Connect to FWA PostgreSQL database

Source: R/lnk_db_conn.R
lnk_db_conn.Rd

Opens a connection to a PostgreSQL database containing fwapg, bcfishpass, and bcfishobs, through fresh::frs_db_conn(), so link and fresh resolve a connection the same way and a bare call to either reaches the same database.

Usage

lnk_db_conn(
  dbname = NULL,
  host = NULL,
  port = NULL,
  user = NULL,
  password = NULL,
  connect_timeout = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

dbname

Database name. Default NULL (resolved as below).

host

Host. Default NULL.

port

Port. Default NULL.

user

User. Default NULL.

password

Password. Default NULL.

connect_timeout

Seconds to wait for each connection attempt, a whole number; 0 waits without limit. Default NULL: PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT when set, otherwise 10. Passed to fresh::frs_db_conn().

...

Further libpq connection keywords, passed to fresh::frs_db_conn() (which sets TCP keepalives by default).

Value

A DBI::DBIConnection object.

Details

Parameters resolve in this order, as fresh::frs_db_conn() resolves them:

  1. Explicit arguments, field by field.

  2. The standard libpq variables (PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD, PGSERVICE, ...). When any of PGHOST, PGHOSTADDR, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER or PGSERVICE is set, libpq resolves every field not given, and the PG_*_SHARE variables are not read.

  3. The legacy PG_*_SHARE variables (PG_DB_SHARE, PG_HOST_SHARE, PG_PORT_SHARE, PG_USER_SHARE, PG_PASS_SHARE), only when none of the standard variables above is set. fresh marks them deprecated and says so once per R session. A call giving all five fields does not read them at all, so it neither prints that message nor uses it up.

  4. libpq's own defaults (the local socket or localhost, the operating system's user name, ~/.pgpass).

The two groups of variables are never mixed. Before link 0.87.0 this function read PG_*_SHARE first and fell back to postgres@localhost:5432 and the database postgis; on a machine setting both groups, a bare call now reaches the PG* target, so pass the arguments to reach the other one.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# The environment's database: PG* variables, else PG_*_SHARE
conn <- lnk_db_conn()
DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)

# A named database: every field given, so the environment fills nothing
conn <- lnk_db_conn(dbname = "fwapg", host = "localhost", port = 5432L,
                    user = "postgres", password = "postgres")
lnk_score(conn, "working.crossings")
DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)

# A slow link: wait longer to connect
conn <- lnk_db_conn(connect_timeout = 30)
DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)
} # }
